assumptions: Only the quote characters inside comments and regex literals change (to a U+0001 stand-in); comment text stays code for the rules and pragmas, as an apostrophe-free comment always read. Rejecting comment text outright would break blackhawk-ignore/savant-ignore pragmas (matched outside strings) and SV004, which fires on comments by design.

Consequence: a rule pattern inside a trailing comment that also holds an apostrophe (`x(); // don't use Date.now()`) now fires, exactly as the same comment without the apostrophe always did. Before, the phantom string hid it by accident.

Lexing is JS-family only (.js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx/.mjs/.cjs and .mts/.cts). Python (`//` is floor division) and PHP (no regex literals) read exactly as before; Python `#`-comment phantoms stay out of scope, since after `#` the rest of the line is comment anyway.

The regex-vs-division decision reuses the shared lib/js-literals.mjs lexer (the engine port from #1193): the previous significant character across lines, not literal line start. `}` is not an expression start there (it mirrors the engine), so `} /x'/` reads as division.

The comment/regex pass runs whole-file in the existing masked twin (maskJsxForFile renamed maskSourceForFile), so a block comment opened on an earlier line counts. blankedRuns ignores the stand-in, so the twin adds no rejected ranges.

ts/src/core/string-literals.ts does NOT share the flaw: it already skips comments (skipComment) and regex literals (regexLiteralEnd). Only its header's stale fidelity note was corrected, plus two pinning tests in ts/test/string-literals.test.ts.
